output.brief: The gap looks mostly like a difference in time in role, not a penalty for working remotely. Remote hiring only opened to all roles in July 2024, so 230 of 340 remote staff (68%) hadn't yet reached the 18 months in level that policy requires for nomination. Only 26% of office staff were in the same position. Among eligible people, nomination rates (28.2% vs 28.6%), approval rates (71% vs 74%) and promotion rates (20.0% vs 21.1%) are nearly the same. The gap also appears in every job family, so job mix doesn't explain it. Remote staff don't leave more often (10.9% vs 11.6%). I'm fairly confident, but the eligible remote group is only 110 people, so a modest real bias can't be ruled out. Stretch-assignment access is untested; manager comments hint at it. Don't adopt the three-day office rule. It rests on a misread comparison and would hit about 180 people hired on home-based contracts. Instead, report promotion rates for eligible staff only and re-check at FY2027. Also check staffing of high-visibility work and clarify promotion criteria, since remote staff report understanding them less.
